title: Review: Photosynthesis overview, pigments and chromatography; Light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle); Limiting factors and rate of photosynthesis; Link reaction and Krebs cycle; Anaerobic respiration; Respiratory substrates and RQ; respirometers
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RS05#t2 term and clue written for the game; PS01b#t2 term and clue written for the game; PS04#t1 term and clue written for the game; PS01b#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: PS01a#N.7a, PS01b#N.9, PS03#N.5, PS04#N.8, RS02#N.3a, RS04#N.11a, RS05#N.10, PS01a#N.4a, PS01b#N.4, PS03#N.2a, PS04#N.3, RS02#N.5. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Potassium hydroxide
items.clue: Alkali solution placed in the tube to absorb CO₂.

items.label: Chlorophyll b
items.clue: The yellow-green photosynthetic pigment separated from a leaf extract.

items.label: Limiting factor
items.clue: The variable in shortest supply, which alone sets the rate of photosynthesis.

items.label: Rf
items.clue: Distance from origin to spot, divided by distance from origin to solvent front.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly matches an adaptation of the chloroplast to its function in photosynthesis?

options.text: The fluid inside the thylakoids contains the enzymes of the Calvin cycle at high concentration.
The stroma holds the photosystems in solution so that light can reach them from every direction.
The thylakoid membranes provide a large surface area in which photosystems are held to absorb light.
The thylakoids enclose a large volume of water to act as the substrate for photolysis.

questions.explanation: Photosystems are embedded in the thylakoid membranes, and their large total area lets many photosystems be packed into one chloroplast.

questions.stem: Illustrative data. On a paper chromatogram of leaf pigments, the origin line was 20 mm from the bottom edge of the paper, the centre of the carotene spot was 65 mm from the bottom edge and the solvent front was 70 mm from the bottom edge. What is the Rf value of carotene?
questions.explanation: Pigment: 65 − 20 = 45 mm. Solvent front: 70 − 20 = 50 mm. Rf = 45 ÷ 50 = 0.90.

questions.stem: What is required to convert glycerate 3-phosphate into triose phosphate in the Calvin cycle?

options.text: ATP only; the reduced NADP is saved for the later regeneration of RuBP from triose phosphate.
Reduced NADP only; ATP from the light-dependent reactions is not used in the light-independent reactions.
A second molecule of carbon dioxide, which Rubisco attaches to glycerate 3-phosphate.
ATP, which phosphorylates glycerate 3-phosphate, and reduced NADP, which reduces it.

questions.explanation: Both products of the light-dependent reactions are used: ATP supplies energy and a phosphate group; reduced NADP supplies the hydrogen for the reduction.

questions.stem: A student places a lamp at different distances from a beaker of pondweed in sodium hydrogencarbonate solution kept at 25 °C, and counts the bubbles of gas released per minute at each distance. Which correctly identifies the variables?

options.text: Independent: lamp distance; dependent: bubbles per minute
Independent: bubbles per minute; dependent: distance of lamp
Controlled variable: lamp distance; dependent: bubbles per minute
Independent: temperature of 25 °C; dependent: bubbles per minute

questions.explanation: Lamp distance is deliberately changed (it sets light intensity): independent. Bubble count is measured: dependent. Temperature and hydrogencarbonate concentration are controlled.

questions.stem: What happens to pyruvate in the link reaction of aerobic cell respiration?

options.text: It enters the Krebs cycle directly, where it combines with oxaloacetate to form citrate.
It reacts with oxygen in the matrix, forming carbon dioxide and a two-carbon acetyl group that enters the cycle.
It is oxidised and decarboxylated to a 2C acetyl group, which coenzyme A carries to the Krebs cycle.
It is bound by coenzyme A, the enzyme that catalyses its conversion into citrate in the matrix.

questions.explanation: Pyruvate loses carbon dioxide (decarboxylation) and hydrogen (oxidation, reducing NAD). The acetyl group is bound to coenzyme A and transferred to the cycle.

questions.stem: Crucian carp can survive for months in ice-covered ponds with no oxygen. In these conditions their muscle cells convert pyruvate to ethanol and carbon dioxide, and the ethanol leaves through the gills. Which statement about this anaerobic respiration is correct?

options.text: It takes place inside the mitochondria, which is where the ethanol is made.
All its ATP comes from glycolysis: far less per glucose than aerobic respiration.
Converting pyruvate to ethanol releases extra ATP, which is why the fish survives.
It still uses the small amount of oxygen that remains dissolved in the pond water.

questions.stem: Illustrative data. A student measured oxygen uptake by yeast (cm³ g⁻¹ min⁻¹) at five temperatures: 20 °C 0.10; 30 °C 0.19; 40 °C 0.31; 50 °C 0.26; 60 °C 0.04. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Rate rises with temperature over the whole range, so the low reading at 60 °C must be an experimental error.
Rate rises with temperature up to an optimum near 40 °C, then falls as the enzymes of respiration denature.
Above 40 °C the yeast switches to anaerobic respiration, which uses no oxygen, so oxygen uptake falls.
At 60 °C the extra carbon dioxide produced expands and pushes the liquid back, hiding the true rate.

questions.stem: Glucose produced by photosynthesis contains hydrogen atoms. From which substance were these hydrogen atoms obtained?

options.text: Carbon dioxide molecules joined together to make glucose.
Water molecules, which are split during photosynthesis.
Mineral ions the roots absorbed from the soil water.
Chlorophyll, which breaks down during the reaction.

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is converted to glucose using hydrogen obtained by splitting water. The oxygen left over from the split water molecules is released.

questions.stem: The absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a has peaks at about 430 nm (blue) and 660 nm (red) but a trough at about 550 nm (green). Which statement best explains this pattern?

options.text: Green photons carry too little energy to excite an electron in chlorophyll a, whereas blue and red photons both carry more than enough energy to do so.
Chlorophyll a absorbs green light more strongly than any other colour, which is exactly why leaves that contain it appear green.
Blue and red light heat the chlorophyll molecule more than green light does, so more of their energy is taken in and stored.
Only photons whose energy matches that needed to excite an electron in chlorophyll a are absorbed; blue and red photons match, green do not.

questions.stem: A student is drawing a model of how the two stages of photosynthesis in a chloroplast are connected. Which set of arrows between the light-dependent stage and the Calvin cycle should the model show?

options.text: ATP and reduced NADP from the light-dependent stage to the Calvin cycle; no arrow going back to it
ATP and reduced NADP from the light-dependent stage to the Calvin cycle; ADP, Pᵢ and NADP back
ATP and reduced NADP from the Calvin cycle to the light-dependent stage; ADP, Pᵢ and NADP back again
Absorbed light energy from the light-dependent stage to the Calvin cycle; no arrow going back

questions.stem: Pondweed submerged in water at 25 °C with the carbon dioxide concentration of ordinary air was exposed to increasing light intensity. The rate of photosynthesis rose at first and then levelled off, staying constant however much the light intensity was increased. Which change is most likely to raise the rate at this plateau?

options.text: Moving the lamp even closer, so that the light intensity becomes higher still.
Adding sodium hydrogencarbonate to the water to raise the carbon dioxide concentration.
Nothing, because the plateau is the maximum rate of which the plant is capable.
Adding more water to the beaker, since water is a reactant in photosynthesis.

questions.stem: One acetyl group enters the Krebs cycle and oxaloacetate is regenerated. Which account of one turn of the cycle is correct?

options.text: Two decarboxylations give off carbon dioxide, four dehydrogenations reduce carriers, one ATP forms.
Two carbon dioxide molecules form when oxygen oxidises the carbon atoms of the acetyl group directly.
Each of the four oxidations forms one ATP directly, so the cycle yields most of the cell's ATP supply.
Only decarboxylation occurs, since no oxygen enters the matrix to oxidise any of the cycle's intermediates.

questions.explanation: Per turn, two carbons leave as carbon dioxide, four oxidations by removal of hydrogen produce reduced carriers (mainly reduced NAD), and one ATP forms directly.
